name: Hula Valley (Hula Nature Reserve and Agamon Hula)
blurb: A restored Rift Valley marsh where cranes, pelicans and jackals share reeds and springs.

tip.title: Drain the springs
tip.text: The old Lake Hula was drained in the 1950s. Cut the water to -100% and watch the reeds, papyrus and fish fade, then the pelicans, otters and cranes that rely on them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A tall wetland grass that forms dense reedbeds along marsh edges and channels. Coypu and mallards are recorded feeding on it.

nodes.name: Narrow-leaf cattail
nodes.desc: A tall emergent marsh plant of shallow, still water that gives cover and food to waterbirds and fish.
A creeping grass of damp meadows and field edges around the valley. Wild boar and mallards are recorded eating it.
A common dabbling duck of the open water and marsh edges. Recorded eating reed and Bermuda grass, and itself prey for jungle cats, otters and harriers.
A large semi-aquatic rodent from South America that now lives in the valley wetlands and eats reed and other water plants.

nodes.name: Carp and tilapia
nodes.desc: Fish of the lake and channels. Remains show that carp, tilapia and catfish lived in old Lake Hula, and pelicans and otters hunt fish here today.
Tens of thousands stop over in the valley each year on the flyway from Finland to Africa. It eats mostly plants and waste grain, with some animal food.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots in wet soil and eats plants, eggs and carrion. It is among the most recorded large mammals of the valley.
Its larvae live in still water and feed on microbes and detritus, then the adults become food for frogs and other small predators.
Migrating flocks stop in Israel. They feed mainly on fish, often scooping them in groups in shallow water.
A large water frog of ponds and channels that preys on insects and small animals. It is eaten by cats, harriers, otters and jackals.
A raptor that hunts low over reedbeds for frogs and waterbirds.
A semi-aquatic hunter of fish and frogs, recorded in the valley waterways.
The reed cat favours wetlands with dense reeds and hunts rodents, birds, frogs and fish.
An opportunistic hunter and scavenger of rodents, birds, frogs, reptiles, fruit and carrion. It is common in the valley.
Top predator of the region, hunting gazelle and boar. Wolves dominate jackals where they meet.
Warm, bright weather drives plant growth in the valley.

nodes.name: Springs and water level
nodes.desc: Perennial springs feed the marsh. Draining the old lake in the 1950s shows how much the web depends on water.

nodes.name: Peat soil
nodes.desc: Peat and wet soils form where the marsh stays flooded, and they dried and burned after drainage.
Microbes and invertebrates that break down dead reed and carcasses into nutrients.

link_ideas.with: Great Rift Valley flyway (Finland to Ethiopia)
link_ideas.what: Common cranes and many other migratory birds stop in the Hula Valley on the Rift Valley flyway.
